slides.heading: Smallest Difference
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Smallest Difference, a medium arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Pick one number from each array with the smallest absolute difference; return [a, b].
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Pick one number from each array with the smallest absolute difference; return a, b .

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Sort both arrays, then walk them together, always advancing the smaller value to close the gap.
slides.narration: Sort both arrays, then walk them together, always advancing the smaller value to close the gap.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Sort both + two pointers → O(n log n + m log m)
Moving the larger value can only widen the gap
slides.narration: Checking every pair costs n times m. After sorting both arrays, two pointers walk forward, always advancing the smaller value, because moving the larger one can only make the difference bigger.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Compare current values and record the gap
3. Advance the pointer at the smaller value
slides.narration: Step by step. First, sort both. Second, compare current values and record the gap. Third, advance the pointer at the smaller value. Fourth, stop early on zero.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We sort both arrays, then loop while both pointers are in range. We compute the absolute difference as a long, keep the best pair, and advance whichever side is smaller, breaking on an exact match.

slides.heading: Complexity
bullets: Time: O(n log n + m log m)
slides.narration: Time is O of n log n plus m log m. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: If the values are equal, the difference is zero and we can stop. Use a long for the subtraction to avoid overflow.

bullets: Explain why advancing the smaller is safe
slides.narration: Explain clearly why moving the smaller pointer never misses the answer.

bullets: Sort both arrays, then walk them together, always advancing the smaller value to close the gap.
Complexity: O(n log n + m log m)
